```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)

batting_2021 <- read_csv("batting2021.csv") |> mutate(Season = 2021L)
batting_2022 <- read_csv("batting2022.csv") |> mutate(Season = 2022L)
all_batting <- bind_rows(batting_2021, batting_2022)
```

Welcome! What makes an elite college softball offense—putting the bat on the ball, swinging for the fences, stealing every base in sight, or landing a star from the transfer portal? Using **4,406 individual player-seasons** across **302 NCAA Division I programs** from the 2021 and 2022 seasons, this site lets you dig into the stories and interactive tools behind modern college softball hitting.

## College Softball's Best Lineups (2021–2022)

Before diving into individual players, hover over the bars below to see the **15 strongest single-season college lineups** of 2021 and 2022, ranked by plate-appearance-weighted `OPS` (On-Base Plus Slugging, which combines getting on base with hitting for extra bases). Back-to-back national champion **Oklahoma** holds the top two spots by a wide margin.

```{r}
top_teams <- all_batting |>
  group_by(Team, Season) |>
  summarise(
    team_OPS = weighted.mean(OPS, PA),
    team_BA = sum(H) / sum(AB),
    total_HR = sum(HR),
    total_SB = sum(SB),
    players = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(players >= 7) |>
  slice_max(order_by = team_OPS, n = 15) |>
  mutate(
    TeamSeason = paste0(Team, " ('", substr(as.character(Season), 3, 4), ")"),
    TeamSeason = fct_reorder(TeamSeason, team_OPS)
  )

p_teams <- top_teams |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = team_OPS,
    y = TeamSeason,
    fill = factor(Season),
    text = paste0(
      "<b>", Team, " (", Season, ")</b>",
      "<br>Weighted OPS: ", sprintf("%.3f", team_OPS),
      "<br>Team Batting Avg: ", sprintf("%.3f", team_BA),
      "<br>Home Runs: ", total_HR,
      "<br>Stolen Bases: ", total_SB
    )
  )) +
  geom_col(width = 0.72) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("2021" = "#1d4ed8", "2022" = "#b91c1c"),
    name = "Season"
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.85, 1.32)) +
  labs(
    title = "Top 15 NCAA D1 Softball Offenses by Weighted OPS (2021–2022)",
    x = "Lineup Weighted OPS (On-Base + Slugging)",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggplotly(p_teams, tooltip = "text", height = 470) |>
  layout(margin = list(t = 60, b = 55, l = 135, r = 25))
```

- **[Players](players.qmd) *(Interactive Explorer)*:** Search all 3,200+ players and 302 colleges across 2021 and 2022, complete with school crests, transfer badges, and combined career lines.
- **[Hitting Graphs](hitting.qmd) *(Interactive Explorer)*:** Test how strikeouts (`K`) affect batting average (`BA`) across both seasons and hover to inspect outliers.
- **[Power Hitting](story.qmd) *(Data Story)*:** Discover why home-run power normally costs strikeouts—and how Oklahoma's Jocelyn Alo and Tiare Jennings broke that rule completely.
- **[Transfers & Breakouts](transfers.qmd) *(Story + Explorer)*:** Follow the 72 players who switched Division I colleges between 2021 and 2022, compare them with 1,063 returning teammates, and browse the biggest year-over-year breakouts.
- **[Speed & Power](speed.qmd) *(Story + Explorer)*:** See why college runners succeed on 83.5% of steal attempts on 60-foot basepaths, and meet the ultra-rare "15 HR / 15 SB" club.
